page.layout: One page of running text in a single column. Page number "188" at the top left. Running head "De sana, sive recta Ratione." centred at the top. No marginal notes. Catchword "Judicii" at the right below the last line. A fragment of the neighbouring page shows at the right edge and is omitted.

main_text.p: eamve immuant. Inter quæ & ille est à Domino Iesu explicatus, Ego Deus Abrahami & Deus Isaaci &c. Sic ille, Epist. 3. ad Dudith. p. 507. Col. 2. Tom. 1. Unde Frantz. non immerito illum sic redarguit. — Non me latet, Te etiam negare immortalitatem Animarum, nisi Christianorum in Resurrectione. Et videbimus infra Te confugere ad impium Dogma Epicureorum, ut eorum Patrocinio Te tegas. Puccii Def. ad Resp. Socini, Præfat: p. 264. col. 2. in fine. Tom. 2. Catech. Rac. in eandem sententiam — Homo natura nihil habet commune cum Immortalitate. pag. 15. Smalcius quidem contra Frantzium, videri vult, contra morem suum, paulo modestior in hoc Dogmate asserendo, dum se credere dicit, Animas vel spiritus Hominum post mortem redire ad Deum, & ita suo modo esse superstites. Disp. de extr. Judic. Sect: 4. Interea tamen, ad ista loca quæ ad immortalitatem animarum asserendam affert Frantzius. Responsa qualiacunque potest, reddit; istaque loca invalida esse affirmat ad probandum illud, cujus gratia afferuntur. Idem Ib. Sect. 3. a- pertius sensum suum de hac Re profert, cum ait — An Spiritus ille, qui ad Deum redit, & a Corpore separatus est, sensu aliquo præditus sit, & an voluptate aliqua fruatur ante Adventum Christi, & ante conjunctionem illam novam sui cum Corpore glorificato, quod Deus olim daturus est credentibus, valde dubitamus; imo aliter se habere credimus. Nempe quemadmodum Corpus sine Spiritu, Cadaver est: ita vicissim, Spiritus sine Corpore, nullas actiones exercere potest. Idem, Exam. 100. Err. Anima Sanctorum, post mortem, nihil sentiunt, nec aliqua Re perfruuntur, cum sine Corpore nullas operationes exercere possint. Err. 81. & in Exam. 157. Err. Anima Sanctorum, ante Diem Judicii

page.notes: The first word "immuant" and the second word "affert" are read with some doubt; the scan is blurred there. The text is printed as set; "Responsa" and "potest" are a possible misreading of the line break and are read as printed. The line ends with the catchword "Judicii" at the right, which is not repeated in the text. The reading of the mid-line hyphen in "a- pertius" follows the printed line end.
